title: UK bill to implement EU deal will allow ministers to enact closer ties in future
summary_full: Further deals can be enacted via same legislation, though it excludes rejoining single market, customs union or bloc as a wholeA bill to implement the UK-EU deal will grant significant powers for ministers to enact even closer ties with Brussels, though it will stop short of Labour’s red lines.The government put what it is calling the “cutting costs bill” before parliament on Thursday, beginning the legislation to put the deal into law after it was agreed with the EU last Friday – though the deal to ease access for food and drink exports will not come into force until 2028, with the emissions trading deal to follow that year.
